In ''[[Age of Empires IV]]'', [[resource]]s are the primary form of currency that players use to create [[Unit (Age of Empires IV)|units]], construct [[Building (Age of Empires IV)|buildings]], research [[Technology (Age of Empires IV)|technologies]], and advance through the Ages. Gathering resources and managing an economy is one of the game's fundamental aspects. == Overview == ''Age of Empires IV '' features four main resources: [[food]], [[wood]], [[gold]], and [[stone]]. Each of the resources has a different primary purpose: * [[File:Food AoE4.png|22px]] '''{{Resources|Food}}''' is required to create almost every [[Unit type (Age of Empires IV)#Human|human]] and [[Ship (Age of Empires IV)|naval]] unit. It is also the primary resource required to advance in Age, and is also used to research many different technologies. * [[File:Wood AoE4.png|22px]] '''{{Resources|Wood}}''' is the primary resource used to construct buildings - only a small number do not require it. It is also one of the main resources required to build all ships and [[siege engine]]s, and many basic human units like the [[Spearman (Age of Empires IV)|Spearman]], [[Archer (Age of Empires IV)|Archer]], [[Horseman]], and unique equivalents. It is also used to research some technologies. * [[File:Gold AoE4.png|22px]] '''{{Resources|Gold}}''' is required to research almost every technology in the game. It is also the secondary resource required to advance in Age. Many powerful units, such as [[Unit type (Age of Empires IV)#Heavy|heavy units]] and siege engines, require gold to create. * [[File:Stone AoE4.png|22px]] '''{{Resources|Stone}}''' is the resource with the fewest uses and thus is typically the most scarce on almost all maps. It is required primarily for the construction of strong [[Defensive structure#Age of Empires IV|defensive buildings]], as well as various other unique buildings. In a standard game, players start out with only a small amount of resources and must gather additional resources to build up their economy and military. For most [[Civilization (Age of Empires IV)|civilizations]], the exact amount is {{Resources|food = 200|wood = 150|gold = 100}} but some civilizations can have slightly more or less of one resource. There are three primary methods of gathering resources: * Using specific [[Unit type (Age of Empires IV)#Workers|worker units]] to gather from natural resources on the map * Through various forms of passive resource generation * Using specific worker units to [[Trade (Age of Empires IV)|trade]] with allied players or neutral Trade Posts. [[File:Resource UI AoE4.png|thumb|The resource UI showing the amount of resources and gathers, as well as the amount of food per minute]]The amount of resources a player has collected is displayed in the bottom left corner of the UI, with each resource shown alongside the amount of workers gathering from it. Resource income rates in terms of amount per minute can be displayed by hovering the cursor over each resource. Resources are always displayed to the nearest integer, but are actually collected and stored to some number of decimal points. In rare cases, this can result in not being able to perform an action despite seemingly having enough resources according to the UI (for example, not being able to build a 150-wood building because the player only has 149.5 wood). In addition to the [[Town Center (Age of Empires IV)|Town Center]], which can accept any resource, each resource type has its own dedicated drop-off site. Food is dropped off at the [[Mill (Age of Empires IV)|Mill]] and [[Dock (Age of Empires IV)|Dock]], wood is dropped off at the [[Lumber Camp (Age of Empires IV)|Lumber Camp]], and gold and stone are dropped off at the [[Mining Camp (Age of Empires IV)|Mining Camp]]. Once resources have been gathered, they can also be exchanged for each other at the [[Market (Age of Empires IV)|Market]]. === Additional resources === In addition to the four main resources, certain civilizations have unique resources or 'currency' that can be accumulated through in-game actions and spent for various purposes. * {{Resources|Olive Oil}}: The only one that is referred to as an actual resource and displayed alongside the other resources in the UI. Olive oil is gathered by the [[Byzantines (Age of Empires IV)|Byzantines]] exclusively as extra income from certain types or resource nodes. It is used exclusively to hire [[Mercenary House|mercenaries]], which are other civilizations' unique units. Olive oil can also be bought and sold at the Market and obtained through trading. * '''Experience''': [[Jeanne d'Arc]] earns experience through fighting with its titular [[Jeanne d'Arc (hero)|hero unit]] and can use this experience to upgrade her. The Ottomans also collect [[Imperial Council|experience]] from creating units and advancing through the Ages, and can use it to send units or unlock various bonuses. * {{Resources|Silver}}: Gathered and used exclusively by the [[Macedonian Dynasty]] as their unique resource. This replaces the Olive Oil resource which is used by their base civilization, the Byzantines. == Natural resources == Every map contains different amounts of resource nodes containing one of the primary resources in different amounts. There are no resource nodes that contain more than one type of resource, although some civilizations have bonuses which can passively grant them a secondary resource as they gather from a resource node. Resources are collected from these nodes by assigning worker units to gather from them, specifically [[Villager (Age of Empires IV)|Villagers]] and [[Fishing Boat (Age of Empires IV)|Fishing Boats]] (for water resources only). The following is a summary of all natural resource sources available in the game. Additional information is located on each of the resource's individual page. === Food sources === Food is the only resource which can be gathered from multiple natural resource nodes on the map. These are as follows: ; [[File:AoE4 Sheep.png|22px]] [[Sheep#Age of Empires IV|Sheep]] Sheep are the most immediate source of food for every civilization, and each one contains {{Resources|food = 200}}. In a standard game, almost every civilization starts out with five Sheep and must collect additional Sheep from around the map using [[Scout (Age of Empires IV)|Scouts]]. The [[Mongols (Age of Empires IV)|Mongols]] can also create Sheep through their [[Pasture (Age of Empires IV)|Pastures]]. ; [[File:AoE4 BerryBush.png|22px]] [[Berry Bush#Age of Empires IV|Berry Bushes]] Berry Bushes, or simply berries, are another source of food available to all civilizations, and players will almost always start out with one 'safe' patch within range of their [[Capital Town Center]]. They contain {{Resources|food = 250}} each and usually spawn in a few patches of six or eight bushes. More rarely, they can also spawn in small 'straggler' groups of two, usually distributed in greater number over a wider area in this case. ; [[File:AoE4 Deer.png|22px]] [[Deer#Age of Empires IV|Deer]] Deer are typically a secondary source of food, usually appearing farther away from the Capital Town Center in small, medium, large, or extra large packs of three, five, seven, and ten respectively. Each Deer has {{Resources|food = 350}}, and they are usually [[hunt]]ed after food from nearby Sheep and berries has been exhausted. After researching [[Professional Scouts]], [[Scout (Age of Empires IV)|Scouts]] can pick up Deer and bring them back to a player's base, reducing the risk of gathering from them, but at the cost of a slow decay of food while they are being carried. ; [[File:AoE4 Boar.png|22px]] [[Boar#Age of Empires IV|Boar]] The Boar is the highest risk but highest reward source of food. With {{Resources|food = 2,400}}, they contain more food than any other source, and have the fastest gather rate. However, they also fight back if attacked, and have high enough hit points, armor, and attack to easily defeat small groups of Villagers. There are usually only a few on each map located in contestable areas between teams. ; [[File:AoE4 Fish.png|22px]] [[Shore Fish#Age of Empires IV|Shoreline Fish]] Shoreline Fish are present on the shores of most bodies of water, whether deep or shallow, and are gatherable by both Villagers and Fishing Boats. They contain {{Resources|food = 600}}. ; [[File:AoE4 Fish.png|22px]] [[Fishing#Age of Empires IV|Deep Water Fish]] Deep Water Fish can appear in the middle of larger bodies of deep water, and are gatherable only by Fishing Boats. They initially contain {{Resources|food = 1,000}}, but slowly respawn after being depleted, resulting in an infinite source of food. === Other resources === All other resources can only be obtained from a single type of resource node: ; [[File:AoE4 gaia tree prototype.png|22px]] [[Tree#Age of Empires IV|Trees]] - Wood Wood can only be obtained from the map by from chopping trees. All trees contain {{Resources|wood = 150}} and have the same gather rate. Trees are present in both dense forests, which can not be bypassed, in Stealth Forest, which can be bypassed but restrict [[Line of Sight]], or as lone stragglers. ; [[File:AoE4 GoldDeposit.png|22px]] [[Gold Mine#Age of Empires IV|Gold Veins]] - Gold Gold can only be gathered from gold deposits. These exist in Tiny, Small, and Large deposits of {{Resources|gold = 1,600}}, {{Resources|gold = 4,000}}, and {{Resources|gold = 8,000}} respectively. ; [[File:AoE4 StoneDeposit.png|22px]] [[Stone Mine#Age of Empires IV|Stone Outcroppings]] - Stone Similarly, stone can only be gathered from stone deposits. These exist in Small and Large deposits of {{Resources|stone = 1,200}} and {{Resources|stone = 2,400}} respectively. === Special resource nodes === ; [[File:Meteorite AoE4.png|22px]] [[Meteorite]] - Gold and Stone This resource is essentially a combination of a Gold Vein and Stone Outcropping, and can only be found on the random map [[Craters]] as well as in the [[Crucible]] game mode. It contains {{Resources|gold = 4,000|stone = 4,000}}, and Villagers gather both resources simultaneously. == Created resources == In addition to gathering resources from naturally available nodes on the map, there are ways for the player to generate their own resource nodes that can be worked by Villagers. These typically have some upfront resource cost, making them more suitable in the mid-to-late game. They can be infinite or exhaustible. ; {{4icons|Cattle}} - Food Cattle can only be created by [[Malians (Age of Empires IV)|Malian]] players from their Mill, costing {{Resources|gold = 90}}. They are herdable animals that can be gathered from just like Sheep, and contain {{Resources|food = 500}}. Once created by the Malian player, any civilization's Villagers can gather from them. ; {{4icons|Farm}}s - Food Farms are the standard food source for almost all civilizations in the mid-to-late game, once natural resources on the map have been exhausted or once they become more difficult to obtain. They are constructed by Villagers and then can be harvested to provide infinite food, as long as they are not destroyed. ; [[File:Reindeer Icon AoE4.png|22px]] '''[[Reindeer#Age of Empires IV|Reindeer]]''' Reindeer are only available to the [[Jin Dynasty]]. They start out with two under their Town Center, and an additional four can be spawned by researching [[Collective Hunting]]. ; {{4icons|Stockyard}} - Food The equivalent of Farms for the [[Golden Horde]]. They can be worked by four Villagers at a time, and also act as their own drop-off site. ; [[File:TokoKojiMats AoE4.png|22px]] '''[[Sake Brewery#Toko-Koji Mats|Toko-Koji Mats]]''' Toko-Koji mats are only available in a limited number from the [[Sake Brewery]] of the [[Sengoku Daimyo]]. They are essentially a Farm equivalent for gold, able to be worked by Villagers to provide an infinite amount. == Resource gather rates == {| class="fandom-table" !Resource !Amount !Base Gather Rate

The number and placement of each resource on each map depend on many variables, including the number of players, the map size, and even sometimes the map biome. Resources on the map can roughly be divided into 'starting' resources and 'distributed' resources, which themselves can be either 'accessible' or 'contested' depending on the way they are defined by the map generation script. === Starting resources === Starting resources are resources 'assigned' to each player and tied specifically to the player's start position. At least one node of each resource type is usually within range of the player's Capital Town Center to provide them a relatively un-raidable early source of that resource. This is in addition to the five Sheep that every player starts with belonging to them, which are not generated by the map script but rather assigned separately along with the Villagers and other units. The 'standard' starting resource nodes are: * Four nearby individual Sheep (along with the five starting Sheep at the Town Center) * One medium Berry Bush patch within range and a secondary one further out * One large Deer pack typically outside of the starting Line of Sight * One close small Gold Vein and a secondary one further out * One close small Stone Outcropping and a secondary one further out * One or two large circular woodlines The actual starting resources can vary from map to map. For example, [[Prairie#Age of Empires IV|Prairie]] and [[Turtle Ridge]] both have large starting Gold Veins and Stone Outcroppings. Quite a few maps like [[Continental#Age of Empires IV|Continental]], [[Cliffside]], [[Dry Arabia]], and [[Rocky River]] have additional nearby Sheep, especially after [[patch 16.2.10604]]. [[Marshland]] has large starting Berry Bushes while [[Forest Ponds]] only has stragglers. Several maps like [[Baltic#Age of Empires IV|Baltic]] and [[Atacama#Age of Empires IV|Atacama]] have each player starting with a nearby Boar, while other maps like [[Altai]] or [[Hideout#Age of Empires IV|Hideout]] move the starting Deer to within the radius of the Capital Town Center. In general, the greater the amount of starting resources, the longer a player will be able to keep their Villagers within range of their Town Center, and the safer it will be to play defensively or perform fast castle strategies. The positioning of the starting resources can also often have an impact on the game. For example, 'forward' resources (closer to the opponent) are more susceptible to tower rushing strategies and may require more investment to defend. === Distributed resources === The rest of the resources outside the starting ones are usually distributed randomly across the map through an algorithm, although on some maps, like [[Canal]], there may be resource nodes deliberately placed in specific areas of the map by the map script. The number of these distributed resources will always vary depending on the map size and player number, and they can either be placed in 'contestable' or 'accessible' areas. The former will usually be placed more densely around the middle of the area between teams, whereas the latter will be closer to one team, although each area can be defined individually for each map. All distributed resources are excluded from spawning too close to the Capital Town Center. The total number of distributed resource combinations between maps is far too many to list, but many maps, especially from the base game, have a standard number of distributed resources, which is as follows: * Standard Sheep distributions. Either: ** Two accessible individual Sheep per player and one contested group of three per player, except in 1 vs 1s where the group of three is replaced with one contested and one accessible group of two per player OR ** Two contested Sheep per player plus two additional default Sheep{{tt|*|This distribution was added on several maps with patch 16.2.10604}} * One accessible large Berry Bush patch per player * One additional accessible large Deer pack per player * Two contested Boars and large Gold Veins in 1 vs 1, plus 1 for each successively larger map size * One accessible large Stone Outcropping per player * One accessible small Gold Vein and Stone Outcropping per player, plus two to four contested of each depending on the map size. Thus a land map with standard starting and distributed resources has the following amount of resources per player. For example, most naval maps have an increased amount of gold and wood to support the creation of ships, in addition to the large or infinite amount of extra food from the fish sources. Maps with less wood such as Prairie may make it more difficult to support Archer-heavy armies, while maps with less gold like [[Himeyama]] or Carmel disadvantage expensive unit combinations or incentivize trade. Different resource distributions can also give a greater advantage to specific civilizations. For example, maps with more berries like [[Lipany]] are beneficial for the [[Abbasid Dynasty]] or [[Delhi Sultanate]], while maps with more hunt like [[Haywire]] can benefit [[Rus]]. == Passive resource generation == The term 'passive resource generation', while not explicitly defined, is often used to refer to any source of resources that does not require direct gathering by a Villager or other worker unit, and/or generates resources independently from the natural resources on the map. This form of resource generation is particularly valuable because it usually does not require extra economic population space to gather, leaving additional room for military units. Additionally, in many cases it can be kept close to a player's base, making it less susceptible to enemy map control and raiding. Passive resource generation may require an initial investment such as constructing a building or researching a technology, or it may be part of a landmark or civilization bonus. It may initially have some dependence on natural resource nodes, such as with the [[Hunting Cabin]] or [[Pit Mine]], but the resource generation is usually infinite after that. The primary exception to this rule is the [[Mongols (Age of Empires IV)|Mongol]] [[Ovoo]], which extracts stone from the Stone Outcropping on which it is built, and expires along with the node. Some forms of passive resource generation may indirectly require some unit to gather it, including tax collection for the [[Chinese (Age of Empires IV)|Chinese]] and [[Zhu Xi's Legacy]], [[Enclosures]], and the [[Golden Tent#Edicts|Stockyard Edict]]. In these cases, the actual resources are generated by buildings, and not the worker units themselves. Passive resource generation is usually in the form of a small, steady resource trickle over time, but it can also be given as larger amounts of resources available periodically. Passive resources do not include secondary resources generated by gathering resources normally from natural resource nodes. Examples of this include the [[Japanese (Age of Empires IV)|Japanese]] civilization bonus granting extra stone with gold mining and vice versa, or the Byzantine olive oil bonus. These essentially amount to a resource gathering bonus similar to what would be obtained from researching a technology. They also do not include resources generated by active abilities, such as [[Cistern of the First Hill#Macedonian Dynasty|Cistern's Favor]], since even though these resources are not gathered by Villagers and are independent of natural resource nodes, they require active player input to obtain (and are thus inherently not 'passive'). {{Resources|stone = 25}}/min |- |[[Zhu Xi's Legacy#Taxes|Taxes]] |{{Resources|gold = Variable}}/min |} == Changelog == * Originally, Deep Water Fish and Shoreline Fish contained {{Resources|food = 2,000}} and {{Resources|food = 1,000}} respectively, and had gather rates of 1.1 res/s and 0.75 res/s respectively. With [[patch 11009]], their food amount was reduced to {{Resources|food = 1,000}} and {{Resources|food = 500}} and gather rates to 1 food/s and 0.66 food/s respectively. With the [[Season One Update]], Lodya Fishing Boats gathered from Deep Water Fish and Shoreline Fish at 1.9 food/s and 1.19 food/s respectively. With [[update 6.0.878]], Fishing Boat gather rates were changed to 0.9 food/s and 0.7 food/s, and Lodya Fishing Boat rates were changed to 1.71 food/s and 1.26 food/s for Deep Water and Shoreline Fish respectively. With an unknown patch, the gather rate for Deep Water Fish was further reduced to 0.8 food/s and 1.52 food/s for standard and Lodya Fishing Boats respectively. With [[patch 13.1.4420]], the Deep Water Fish gather rate was reduced to 0.75 food/s and 1.42 food/s for standard and Lodya Fishing Boats respectively, and the Shoreline Fish gather rate was to 0.65 food/s. With [[update 15.1.6970]], the amount of food contained in Shore Fish was increased to {{Resources|food = 600}}, while their gather rates from Fishing Boats and Lodya Fishing Boats were increased to 0.675 and 1.2825 respectively. * Originally, Large and Small Stone Outcroppings contained {{Resources|stone = 3,000}} and {{Resources|stone = 1,500}} respectively. With [[Season Two Update 17718]], they contain {{Resources|stone = 2,400}} and {{Resources|stone = 1,200}} respectively. * Originally, players started with only a single owned Sheep at their Capital Town Center. With [[update 8.0.185]], they start out with three Sheep, and two 'nearby' Sheep were removed from the standard start. With [[Update 11.0.782]], players start out with five owned Sheep. * Originally, Sheep contained {{Resources|food = 250}}. With update 11.0.782, they contain {{Resources|food = 200}} * Originally, Boars contained {{Resources|food = 2,000}}. With [[update 12.0.1974]], they contain {{Resources|food = 2,200}}. With [[update 15.1.6970]], they contain {{Resources|food = 2,400}}. * Originally, the gather rate from Berry Bushes was 0.66 food/s. With update 12.0.1974, it is 0.69 food/s. * With [[update 13.0.4178]], the Tiny Gold Vein was introduced, containing {{Resources|gold = 1,600}} * Originally, Knights Templar wood gather rate was 0.65 wood/s. With patch 13.1.4420, it is 0.63 wood/s * With [[patch 16.2.10604]], the 'standard' Sheep distribution on several maps was changed to be less prone to randomly providing one player a significant advantage over the other in terms of the number of Sheep obtained at the start of the game. On these maps, the number of 'starting' Sheep assigned to each player was increased from four to seven, and the number of neutral Sheep was decreased to two per Player plus two default. Neutral Sheep also no longer spawn in groups of two or three. {{Resource list}} {{Gameplay elements}} [[Category:Resources|*]]
